ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the schematic diagram of the changes in noon solar altitude from April to August at four places of different latitudes in some actual locations (month a is earlier than month b). <image1> What is the correct order of places 1, 2, 3, and 4 in the figure from south to north?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is noon solar altitude, marked with 0°, 60°, and 90°; the vertical direction indicates monthly change, and the stem states that month a is earlier than month b. The four polylines are labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4 respectively. Curve 1 as a whole is closest to the 0° side, and the noon solar altitude is always very low; curve 2 is near 60°, and its solar altitude is obviously higher than 1 but lower than 3 and 4 on the right; curves 3 and 4 are both in the relatively high solar-altitude area, close to or reaching the high-value area, among which 3 and 4 need to be further compared through the position where the maximum value appears and the situation of approaching 90°. Reasoning: From April to August, the direct solar point mainly moves in the Northern Hemisphere. The farther a place is from the direct solar point in the Northern Hemisphere, the lower its noon solar altitude; the closer it is to the direct latitude, the higher the noon solar altitude. Curve 1 is always close to 0°, indicating that it is farthest from the direct solar point in the Northern Hemisphere and should be the southernmost. The height of curve 2 is obviously greater than 1 but less than 3 and 4, so it is north of 1 and south of 3 and 4. Then compare 3 and 4: both are in the high solar-altitude area, but according to the time position when the curve reaches its maximum value or approaches 90°, the direct latitude corresponding to 3 is more northerly, so 3 is north of 4. Therefore, the order of the four places from south to north is 1, 2, 4, 3.

Read the schematic diagram of the changes in noon solar altitude from April to August at four places of different latitudes in some actual locations (month a is earlier than month b).

<image1>

What is the correct order of places 1, 2, 3, and 4 in the figure from south to north?

method.method_draft: 先按图像整体形态分类：曲线1始终靠近0°，说明其在4—8月离北半球直射点最远，应为最南；曲线2的高度明显大于1但小于3、4，排在1以北、3和4以南。再比较3、4：二者都处在高太阳高度区，但根据曲线达到最高值或接近90°的时间位置，3对应的直射纬度更偏北，故3在4以北。于是自南向北为1、2、4、3。

raw_record.original_question:
读4-8月部分实地不同纬度四地正午太阳高度变化示意图（a月早于b月）。

<image1>

图中1、2、3、4四地自南往北的正确排序是什么？
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is noon solar altitude, marked with 0°, 60°, and 90°; the vertical direction indicates monthly change, and the stem states that month a is earlier than month b. The four polylines are labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4 respectively. Curve 1 as a whole is closest to the 0° side, and the noon solar altitude is always very low; curve 2 is near 60°, and its solar altitude is obviously higher than 1 but lower than 3 and 4 on the right; curves 3 and 4 are both in the relatively high solar-altitude area, close to or reaching the high-value area, among which 3 and 4 need to be further compared through the position where the maximum value appears and the situation of approaching 90°.
Reasoning: From April to August, the direct solar point mainly moves in the Northern Hemisphere. The farther a place is from the direct solar point in the Northern Hemisphere, the lower its noon solar altitude; the closer it is to the direct latitude, the higher the noon solar altitude. Curve 1 is always close to 0°, indicating that it is farthest from the direct solar point in the Northern Hemisphere and should be the southernmost. The height of curve 2 is obviously greater than 1 but less than 3 and 4, so it is north of 1 and south of 3 and 4. Then compare 3 and 4: both are in the high solar-altitude area, but according to the time position when the curve reaches its maximum value or approaches 90°, the direct latitude corresponding to 3 is more northerly, so 3 is north of 4. Therefore, the order of the four places from south to north is 1, 2, 4, 3.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Read the schematic diagram of the changes in noon solar altitude from April to August at four places of different latitudes in some actual locations (month a is earlier than month b).

<image1>

What is the correct order of places 1, 2, 3, and 4 in the figure from south to north?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the schematic diagram of the changes in noon solar altitude from April to August at four places of different latitudes in some actual locations (month a is earlier than month b). <image1> What is the correct order of places 1, 2, 3, and 4 in the figure from south to north?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is noon solar altitude, marked with 0°, 60°, and 90°; the vertical direction indicates monthly change, and the stem states that month a is earlier than month b. The four polylines are labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4 respectively. Curve 1 as a whole is closest to the 0° side, and the noon solar altitude is always very low; curve 2 is near 60°, and its solar altitude is obviously higher than 1 but lower than 3 and 4 on the right; curves 3 and 4 are both in the relatively high solar-altitude area, close to or reaching the high-value area, among which 3 and 4 need to be further compared through the position where the maximum value appears and the situation of approaching 90°.
Reasoning: From April to August, the direct solar point mainly moves in the Northern Hemisphere. The farther a place is from the direct solar point in the Northern Hemisphere, the lower its noon solar altitude; the closer it is to the direct latitude, the higher the noon solar altitude. Curve 1 is always close to 0°, indicating that it is farthest from the direct solar point in the Northern Hemisphere and should be the southernmost. The height of curve 2 is obviously greater than 1 but less than 3 and 4, so it is north of 1 and south of 3 and 4. Then compare 3 and 4: both are in the high solar-altitude area, but according to the time position when the curve reaches its maximum value or approaches 90°, the direct latitude corresponding to 3 is more northerly, so 3 is north of 4. Therefore, the order of the four places from south to north is 1, 2, 4, 3.
